setup: Sit upright near the edge of a sturdy chair or bench with both feet flat on the floor.
Lift one leg and rest the outside of that ankle across the opposite thigh, just above the knee, creating a figure-four shape.
Keep the foot of the crossed leg lightly dorsiflexed to protect the knee.
steps: Sit tall with a neutral spine and inhale deeply.
Hinge forward at your hips, bringing your chest toward your crossed shin while keeping your back flat.
Hold the position when you feel a moderate stretch in the outer hip and glute of the crossed leg.
Breathe smoothly and hold for the designated duration before gently returning upright and switching sides.
instructions.breathing: Maintain slow, deep nasal breathing, allowing your hip muscles to relax deeper into the stretch with each exhalation.
cues: Lead with the chest, not the nose.
Hinge from the hips, do not round the back.

common_faults.fault: Rounding through the thoracic or lumbar spine to reach further forward.
common_faults.correction: Keep your chest proud and hinge exclusively from the hips.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the crossed ankle to sickle or roll into extreme inversion.
common_faults.correction: Keep the ankle flexed in slight dorsiflexion to keep the joint stable.

precautions: Avoid forcing the knee downward if you experience sharp knee or hip discomfort; reduce the forward hinge angle.

name: Seated Piriformis Stretch
summary: A seated mobility exercise that targets the deep external rotators of the hip by hinging forward over a crossed leg.
